\caption{Compression, trained on 5\,GB of FineWeb per language (the \texttt{quick} read-until-full sample, which is not uniform over the source), 34{,}685 matched total vocabulary, evaluated on held-out Goldfish. \plainscheme{} is the mean absolute baseline in characters per token, every other compression cell the mean percentage change against it, positive meaning better compression. \bnds{w} $<$ \bnds{wp} $<$ \bnds{wpd} throughout. MorphAlign is IBM1 alignment at threshold 0.01 scaled by 100, MorphScore is $F_1$ with an unsplit word credited rather than dropped; both are on English, and on both higher is better. Gold words are segmented inside a carrier phrase rather than on their own, because a bare word cannot reach a leading-space entry and \plainscheme{} would be scored on splits it does not make in running text. A cell reading $a$/$b$ gives that bare probe before the in-context one, which is the figure ranked; the marker schemes delimit a span the same way either side and the two probes agree for them. \textbf{Bold} is the best and \underline{underline} the runner-up within a column, ties sharing a place; \plainscheme{} ranks at the zero its own percentages are measured from. Per-language numbers in Table~\ref{tab:intrinsic-quick}. Compression figures are means over English, German, Finnish, Russian, Arabic and Korean.}
